en: Form is like a mass of foam; sensation is like a bubble;
perception is like a mirage; mental formations are like the trunk of a plantain tree;
and consciousness is like an illusion.
In the body of a single woman, there arise three conceptualizations: for a wandering mendicant, a lustful man, and a dog, she is respectively a corpse, a mistress, or food.
[This is taught] by means of the teaching on the aggregates, elements, and so forth, in order to bring about the cessation of the grasping at a self.

That [external world] too is destroyed by those of great fortune through the establishment of "mind-only. The teaching of the Sage that "all this is mind-only" is for the sake of removing the fear of the ignorant; it is not from the perspective of ultimate reality.

The Tathāgatas have not perceived a mind characterized by the forms of an awakener and that which is to be awakened. Where there is both an awakener and that which is to be awakened, there awakening is not found.
It is without marks, unarisen, non-abiding, and beyond the reach of speech.
Space and the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) are awakening, characterized by non-duality.
All proponents [of other views] have been terrified by the lion’s roar of emptiness;
just as sweetness is the nature of molasses and heat is the nature of fire.
The emptiness of all phenomena is held to be their suchness. The teachings of the Lords of the World follow the inclinations of sentient beings;
they are divided manifoldly in the world through many skillful means.
Whether distinguished by the division of the profound and the superficial, or possessing both characteristics in some cases,
the teaching— though appearing diverse— is non-different, characterized by the non-duality of emptiness.
